summary: Both sides are the same 1-hour-per-second time-lapse day (night → dawn glow → blue sky with a sun crossing east→west → dusk glow → night) with matching sun trajectory and matching WakeTime/SleepTime dial semantics, but the port's untouched simulated clock starts ~5.7 h later, it kills pixel 0 outright, its sky hue is cyan rather than violet, its twilight windows are narrower, and its Cloudiness dial is effectively broken (moves the wrong way and never occludes the sun).
observations: TIME BASE (both sides, verified): neither side responds to --wall-clock at all. A 24-point sweep of --wall-clock over a full day (1755993600 + h*3600, h=0..23, 4 s @5 fps, dumps at t=0/0.2/2/3.8) produced byte-identical means on BOTH sides at every hour (orig 0.0/0.0/0.0/0.0, port 0.9/6.2/31.2/35.1 at every h). meta.json confirms the flag was applied (settings.wallClock changed per run). So the 'alarm clock' time-of-day input is unobservable from output on either side; the whole day is driven by elapsed render time.

TIME BASE (both sides): the simulated clock advances 1 unit per rendered second (1 h/s). Evidence: with inputNumberSleepTime = 10/14/18/22, the original's day ends at exactly t = 10.5/14.5/18.5/22.5 s (slope 1.000 s per unit) and the port's at t = 4.3/8.3/12.3/16.3 s (same slope, 6 s earlier).

Both sides are TIME-BASED, not frame-coupled: the day's on/off edges sit at exactly the same seconds at --fps 10, 20 and 40 (orig +6.50/-21.50 at all three rates; port +0.50/-15.60..-15.65 at all three).
Both sides are seed-independent: seeds 7 and 1234 produced byte-identical pixel values on each side (cloud texture is deterministic noise, not PRNG).
Both sides run exactly ONE simulated day and then stay black forever — no second sunrise within 130 s at 10 fps (and none within 300 s at 5 fps untouched). Shared behaviour, not a divergence.

UNTOUCHED PHASE OFFSET (divergence): the original's untouched simulated clock starts at hour 0.0 (day lights at t=6.5 s, ends t=21.5 s); the port's starts at hour ~5.7 (day lights at t=0.5 s, ends t=15.65 s). Isolated by the SleepTime sweep: with SleepTime=18 the orig turns off at t=18.5 (origin 0) while the port turns off at t=12.3 (origin 5.7). Untouched, at t=2..7 s the original is still in night (mean 2) while the port is already showing full daylight (mean 36).

The offset disappears the moment WakeTime is dialed: with inputNumberWakeTime = 2/5/8/11 set on BOTH sides, both start at t≈0.2-0.3 s and end at t = 22.2-W / 22.3-W. So the two engines agree on the wake-relative clock origin (wake − 0.5 h) and only the untouched origin differs.

UNTOUCHED GAMMA (divergence): untouched, the ORIGINAL saturates to a flat 255,255,255 on every pixel for its entire day (t=6.5 .. 21.5 s, mean 255 at t=7,8,10,13,16,19,21). Setting sliderGamma to ANY value in 0..1 fixes it (sky becomes 63,63,127 at gamma 0 down to 15,15,63 at gamma 1), so the untouched gamma value sits outside the slider's reachable range. The port untouched renders a normal sky identical to its own gamma=0.5 render (34,49,76). Side effect: the original's five rgbPickers all probe INERT (delta 0.00) purely because its untouched output is clipped white.

UNTOUCHED VIGNETTE (divergence): with only gamma pinned to 0.5, the original's sky is perfectly FLAT across the strip (every pixel 31,31,90, including pixel 0 and pixel 59) while the port has a strong built-in vignette (pixel 0 = 0,0,0, mid ~34,49,76). Day-window mean 63 (orig) vs 31 (port) in the t=10..16 s regime run.

PORT PIXEL 0 IS ALWAYS BLACK: in every dump at every time, every dial setting (including sliderVignette=0), and at both 60 px and 240 px, the port's pixel 0 reads exactly 0,0,0 while the original renders it at full sky colour with Vign=0. Consequence at sunrise: with WakeTime=6/gamma=0.5/Vign=0, at t=0.8 s the original's pixel 0 is the rising sun at 255,255,255; the port's is 0,0,0. Pixel 59 is only dimmed on the port (23,39,67 at Vignette=0), so the darkening is asymmetric — it is not a symmetric vignette.

SKY HUE (divergence): at matched dials (WakeTime=6, Gamma=0.5, Vign/Vignette=0, Cloudiness=0) the original's noon sky is 31,31,90 — R=G, hue 240°, a violet/indigo blue — while the port's is 34,49,76 — R<G<B, hue ~210°, a cyan sky-blue. The original's sky is also spatially uniform; the port's varies 23..35 across the strip even with the vignette slider at 0.

SUN TRAJECTORY MATCHES: with the phase aligned (WakeTime=6 both sides), the sun's brightest pixel is at index 6/12/30/36/54 on the original at t=2/4/8/10/14 s and at 12/30/36/54 on the port at the same times — same left→right (east→west) direction, same ~3 px/s on the 60-px rig, position within ~1 px throughout.

SUN SIZE LAW DIFFERS OFF-DEFAULT: at 60 px both suns are ~3-4 px wide (orig 255,255,255,180; port 115,254,254,67), so the default rig hides it. At --pixels 240 the original's sun is exactly 4 px wide (indices 116-119 at 255, sky 31 on both sides of it) while the port's is ~10 px (indices 111-120 at 254/255). The original's sun is a fixed ~4-px dot; the port's is a fixed FRACTION (~4%) of the strip.
SUN EDGE PROFILE: the original's sun has hard edges (full value then one partial pixel then sky). The port's is feathered on the 60-px rig (115 / 254 / 254 / 67 at t=8) — a soft-edged disc.

CLOUDINESS IS BROKEN ON THE PORT (major dial divergence). Original, Cloudiness 0 → 0.5 → 1 at gamma 0.5/Vign 0: median pixel level 50.7 → 74.7 → 90.0, sky goes from a clean 31,31,90 to a mottled 76,76,90 / 54,54,90 / 84,84,90 and finally to a near-flat overcast 90,90,90, and the sun is OCCLUDED (peak drops from 255,255,255 to 132,132,138). Port over the same sweep: median 56 → 52 → 48 (it slightly DARKENS), sky moves only from 29,49,84 to 36,47,64 / 38,44,54, and the sun stays at 251 with no occlusion at all. Direction, magnitude and sun-occlusion are all wrong.

TWILIGHT WINDOWS ARE NARROWER ON THE PORT. With DawnE/EastDawnColor = pure green and DawnW/WestDawnColor = pure blue, WakeTime=6, gamma 0.5, Vign 0: at dawn the original's east end reads 0,22,0 (t=0.30) → 0,118,0 (t=0.50) → 2,172,19 (t=0.80), still fully in the dawn palette at 0.80; the port reads 0,71,1 → 0,170,4 → 10,113,30, i.e. it has already begun blending to day sky by t=0.80. At dusk the original is fully into its dusk gradient by t=15.30 (23,23,117 at east → 23,57,70 at west) and saturated dusk at t=15.60 (3,3,216 → 3,166,22), while the port still shows the plain day sky at BOTH 15.30 and 15.60 and only reaches the dusk gradient at t=15.90.

DAWN/DUSK GLOW IS PULLED TO THE MIDDLE ON THE PORT: at t=0.5 s (untouched dawn colours, WakeTime=6, Vign/Vignette=0.5) the original's red glow profile across px 0/6/12/18/24/30/36/42/48/54/59 is 33/75/84/79/67/52/36/21/10/2/0 — peaking near px 12 (east). The port's is 0/16/39/57/64/58/44/27/12/3/0 — peaking near px 24-30 (centre). Same at dusk (orig peaks px 48, port px 36).

COLOUR DIAL SEMANTICS CORRESPOND: setting Noon to pure blue on both (rgbPickerNoon=0,0,1 vs hsvPickerNoonSkyColor=0.6667,1,1) gives orig 0,0,90 flat and port 1,1,74..81; pure green gives 0,90,0 and 1,74,1..1,81,1. Setting the sun red (rgbPickerSun=1,0,0 vs hsvPickerSunColor=0,1,1) turns the sun red on both. East/west dawn assignment is the same on both (east end takes DawnE/EastDawnColor). So the pickers map correctly despite the kind mismatch — the port is ~10% dimmer at the same nominal value (81 vs 90 peak).

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH (5 of 11 controls): the original exposes rgbPickerDawnE / rgbPickerDawnW / rgbPickerNoon / rgbPickerSun / rgbPickerClouds (kind rgbPicker); the port exposes hsvPickerEastDawnColor / hsvPickerWestDawnColor / hsvPickerNoonSkyColor / hsvPickerSunColor / hsvPickerCloudColor (kind hsvPicker). Different kind AND different names — a Pixelblaze UI would show colour wheels instead of RGB pickers and different labels. Also sliderVign (orig) vs sliderVignette (port). Only inputNumberWakeTime, inputNumberWeekendWakeTime, inputNumberSleepTime, sliderCloudiness and sliderGamma share names/kinds.

WeekendWakeTime edge case: at inputNumberWeekendWakeTime=2 (gamma 0.5) the ORIGINAL lights a constant dim field (mean 15-16, no motion) from t≈24.1 s (the next simulated day) onward and never turns off through 60 s; the port stays black. At WeekendWakeTime = 10 or 20 neither side reacts. Otherwise this dial is inert on both, checked over a 60 s / 10 fps window covering a full simulated day plus 36 h.

On a 16x16 grid override (gamma 0.5) the original renders a spatially UNIFORM sky (31,31,90 everywhere) plus a single 255,255,255 sun pixel — no vertical structure at all; the port renders a strong vertical gradient (top/bottom rows near 0, middle ~33,47,72) plus a dimmer sun pixel. Same root cause as the vignette/pixel-0 finding, viewed on a 2D rig.
Both sides reach the same terminal state: permanent black after the day ends (both mean 0, motion 0 over t=25..35 s). No dying-port or saturating-port failure mode.

dials.name: WakeTime (inputNumberWakeTime)
dials.origEffect: Sets the simulated clock origin to wake−0.5 h: day starts at t≈0.2 s and ends at t = 22.2−W (W=2→20.2, 5→17.2, 8→14.2, 11→11.2).
dials.portEffect: Identical: day starts at t≈0.3 s, ends at t = 22.3−W (20.3/17.3/14.3/11.3).

dials.name: SleepTime (inputNumberSleepTime)
dials.origEffect: Moves the day's end edge 1 s per unit: S=10/14/18/22 → OFF at t=10.5/14.5/18.5/22.5. Start edge unchanged at t=6.5.
dials.portEffect: Same slope and direction but offset by the clock-origin bug: OFF at t=4.3/8.3/12.3/16.3, start edge at t=0.3.

dials.name: WeekendWakeTime (inputNumberWeekendWakeTime)
dials.origEffect: Inert during the first simulated day; at W=2 only, lights a constant dim field (mean ~16) from t≈24.1 s onward that never ends. W=10/20 do nothing over 60 s.
dials.portEffect: Completely inert at W=2/10/20 over the same 60 s window; never lights after the first day.

dials.name: Cloudiness (sliderCloudiness)
dials.origEffect: 0→1 turns the sky white/overcast with strong per-pixel mottling: median 50.7→74.7→90.0, sky 31,31,90 → 90,90,90, and the sun is occluded (255,255,255 → 132,132,138).
dials.portEffect: 0→1 slightly DARKENS and desaturates: median 56→52→48, sky 29,49,84 → 38,44,54; the sun never dims (stays 251). Wrong direction, ~1/10 the magnitude, no sun occlusion.

dials.name: Vign (orig) / Vignette (port)
dials.origEffect: 0 = perfectly flat strip (pixel 0 = full sky 31,31,90); 0.5 → ends at 7,7,20; 1 → ends at 1,1,4. Symmetric.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and roughly the same depth, but starts from a baked-in vignette: at Vignette=0 pixel 0 is already 0,0,0 and pixel 59 is 26,36,54. Asymmetric and never flat. Control name also differs.

dials.name: Gamma (sliderGamma)
dials.origEffect: 0→1 dims monotonically: sky 63,63,127 → 45,45,107 → 31,31,90 → 22,22,75 → 15,15,63 (blue channel halves). Untouched default lies OUTSIDE this range and clips to 255,255,255.
dials.portEffect: 0→1 dims monotonically: 66,86,114 → 47,65,93 → 34,49,76 → 24,38,63 → 17,29,51 (blue channel ×0.45). Untouched default equals its own gamma=0.5 render.

dials.name: DawnE (orig, rgbPicker) / EastDawnColor (port, hsvPicker)
dials.origEffect: Recolours the east (low-index) end of the dawn glow and the west end of the dusk glow. Pure green → 0,118,0 at px 0 at t=0.5 s.
dials.portEffect: Same east/west assignment and same gradient direction; brighter earlier and exits the dawn palette sooner, and pixel 0 stays black. Control kind (hsvPicker) and name differ.

dials.name: DawnW (orig, rgbPicker) / WestDawnColor (port, hsvPicker)
dials.origEffect: Recolours the west (high-index) end of the twilight gradient; pure blue → 0,0,115 at px 59 at t=0.5 s.
dials.portEffect: Same assignment; glow peak sits nearer the strip centre and the dusk transition arrives ~0.5 simulated hours later. Kind/name differ.

dials.name: Noon (orig, rgbPicker) / NoonSkyColor (port, hsvPicker)
dials.origEffect: Sets the daytime sky colour; pure blue → flat 0,0,90 across the whole strip.
dials.portEffect: Same role; pure blue → 1,1,74..81 with residual spatial variation and a black pixel 0, ~10% dimmer peak. Kind/name differ; untouched hue is 210° vs the original's 240°.

dials.name: Sun (orig, rgbPicker) / SunColor (port, hsvPicker)
dials.origEffect: Colours the travelling sun; pure red → a hard-edged 255,0,x disc ~3-4 px wide at any rig size.
dials.portEffect: Same role and same colour; disc is soft-edged and its width scales with the strip (10 px at 240 px vs the original's 4 px). Kind/name differ.

dials.name: Clouds (orig, rgbPicker) / CloudColor (port, hsvPicker)
dials.origEffect: Not separable from Cloudiness in output (rgbPickerClouds probed 0.00 because the untouched original is clipped white); with Cloudiness up, the cloud tint whitens the sky toward 90,90,90.
dials.portEffect: Probe-responsive (maxDelta 7.87) but the cloud layer it tints is far too weak to matter — see Cloudiness. Kind/name differ.

feedback: Fix the untouched clock origin first — it is the single biggest visible difference. Untouched, the original's simulated day begins at hour 0.0 (strip stays dark for the first 6.5 s of render, sunrise at t=6.5 s, night again at t=21.5 s) while the port begins at hour ~5.7 (already in daylight at t=0.5 s, night at t=15.65 s). Target: with no controls set, the port must be BLACK from t=0 to t=6.5 s and must end its day at t=21.5 s at 1 h per rendered second. Measure with `--seconds 40 --fps 10` and check the meanBrightness on/off edges.

Fix Cloudiness — it is functionally inverted and far too weak. Original at gamma 0.5 / Vign 0 / 60 px: Cloudiness 0 → clean sky, median pixel 50.7; 0.5 → mottled part-cloud, median 74.7, individual pixels swinging between 36,36,90 (clear) and 84,84,90 (cloud); 1.0 → near-flat overcast, median 90.0, sky essentially 90,90,90. Port currently goes 56 → 52 → 48 (darkening) with pixel-to-pixel swings of only a few counts. Clouds must ADD white/grey toward the cloud colour and must be a high-contrast per-pixel field, not a faint tint.
Clouds must occlude the sun. At Cloudiness=1 the original's sun peak drops from 255,255,255 to 132,132,138 (roughly halved); the port's stays at 251 at every cloudiness value.

Pixel 0 is dead on the port at every time, every rig size and every Vignette value including 0 — it reads exactly 0,0,0 while the original renders it at full sky colour. This looks like an x-coordinate/normalisation off-by-one (x = i/(n) giving 0 at the first pixel and feeding a sin/1−|2x−1| style vignette that is never disabled). Two required fixes: (a) Vignette=0 must produce a perfectly FLAT strip (the original is 31,31,90 on every pixel including 0 and 59 at Vign=0); (b) even with the vignette on, the falloff must be symmetric — the original at Vign=0.5 gives 7,7,20 at BOTH ends, the port gives 0,0,0 at px 0 and 26,36,54 at px 59. The visible consequence is that the port loses the rising sun entirely at sunrise (orig px0 = 255,255,255 at t=0.8 s with WakeTime=6).

Correct the noon sky hue. At matched dials the original's untouched noon sky is 31,31,90 — R and G exactly equal, hue 240°, an indigo/violet blue. The port renders 34,49,76 — hue ~210°, visibly cyan. Also make the noon sky spatially FLAT (the original is identical on all 60 pixels at Vign=0; the port varies 23..35).

Widen the twilight windows at both ends. With DawnE=green/DawnW=blue, WakeTime=6, gamma 0.5, Vign 0: the original is still fully in the dawn palette at t=0.80 s (east pixel 2,172,19, i.e. R≈0) whereas the port has already begun mixing day sky by then (10,113,30). At dusk the original has entered its dusk gradient by t=15.30 s and is saturated dusk at t=15.60 s, while the port still draws the plain day sky at both those times and only reaches dusk at t≈15.90 s. The port's twilight is roughly half the original's duration — stretch the dawn/dusk blend windows and start dusk about 0.5 simulated hours earlier.

Move the twilight glow back to the horizon ends. At t=0.5 s the original's dawn glow peaks near pixel 12 (profile 33/75/84/79/67/52/36/21/10/2/0 across px 0/6/12/18/24/30/36/42/48/54/59); the port's peaks near pixel 24-30 (0/16/39/57/64/58/44/27/12/3/0). Same at dusk (orig peaks px 48, port px 36). The glow should hug the east/west ends of the strip, not the centre.

Make the sun a fixed-size dot rather than a strip fraction. At the default 60 px both are ~3-4 px so the default rig hides this, but at --pixels 240 the original's sun is exactly 4 pixels wide (indices 116-119 at 255, sky immediately either side) while the port's is ~10 pixels (111-120). Also the original's disc has hard edges; the port's is feathered (115/254/254/67 at 60 px).

The untouched gamma default: the original untouched clips to 255,255,255 on every pixel for its entire day, while the port untouched renders exactly its own gamma=0.5 look. Since the original's untouched gamma sits outside the 0..1 slider range (gamma=0 gives 63,63,127), the port's untouched brightness is much lower than the original's. Judged mainly on dialed comparisons this is not the headline, but if you want untouched parity the port's default gamma value has to be well below what its own slider's 0 end reaches.

Control-surface parity (fidelity, not appearance): the original exposes five rgbPickers named rgbPickerDawnE / rgbPickerDawnW / rgbPickerNoon / rgbPickerSun / rgbPickerClouds; the port exposes hsvPickers named hsvPickerEastDawnColor / hsvPickerWestDawnColor / hsvPickerNoonSkyColor / hsvPickerSunColor / hsvPickerCloudColor. Both name and kind differ, so a UI shows different widgets and different labels. sliderVign vs sliderVignette is the same problem. Rename and re-kind to match the original's surface.

Neither side reads the pinned wall clock — a 24-hour --wall-clock sweep changes nothing on either side, so this cannot currently be used to verify alarm behaviour. If the original is supposed to read Pixelblaze clock globals, that is an ENGINE-side gap worth a separate ticket; from output, both sides behave as a fixed time-lapse and are consistent with each other on that point.

Minor: at WeekendWakeTime=2 the original lights a constant dim field (mean ~16) from t≈24.1 s (the second simulated day) onward and never turns off; the port stays black. Low priority, but it is the only WeekendWakeTime behaviour visible from output at all.
